neighbours.label: Degree/intensifier word (too, so, rather, more, aussi, trop, настолько, más) immediately before a physical-property adjective, especially heavy/light/weight or size; predicts 'heavy'/'light' next. Multilingual.
fire: We tried to lift the old oak wardrobe, but it was far too heavy for the two of us.
The mine turned out to be so heavy that he had to leave it in the field.
Don't move that cabinet alone; it is rather heavy and you could hurt your back.
My new laptop is somewhat heavier than the old one, but the screen is better.
The backpack was too heavy for the child, so his father carried it up the hill.
This pen is a bit short and quite heavy compared with ordinary pens.
The fossil skull was ten times longer and far heavier than anything found before.
Le sac était trop lourd pour elle, alors elle a demandé de l'aide au chauffeur.
quiet: We tried to lift the old oak wardrobe and finally carried it down the stairs.
He found an old mine in the field and reported it to the police the next morning.
My new laptop has a better screen and a much faster processor than my old one.
The weather was too cold for swimming, so we stayed inside and played cards.
She was so happy about the news that she called her mother right away.
The child carried a red backpack full of books up the hill to school.
The museum displayed a fossil skull found by a team of students last summer.
Il a acheté un nouveau stylo pour écrire des lettres à ses amis.

notes: Label and sentences written blind by a Claude subagent from the card text alone (prompt: haiku_labeler/prompt.md, identical for Haiku, Sonnet and Opus); one retry on mechanical checks. Part of a Haiku/Sonnet/Opus comparison on the same 48 poles.
